questions.q: Will the heir actually occupy Property A as a principal residence within one year of the transfer, and will they file for the homeowners' exemption in that window?
questions.why: Without both, there is no parent-child exclusion at all and the full market value becomes the new taxable value - that is the single biggest swing in the model.
questions.where: Trustee + CPA; county assessor claim BOE-19-P

questions.q: What is the fair market value of Property A on the date of death (retrospective appraisal)?
questions.why: It sets the income-tax basis AND the Prop 19 excess reassessment. A $100k error moves the property-tax projection by about $1,340 a year forever.
questions.where: Licensed appraiser; must be a written, dated report

questions.q: What does a comparable Santa Clara County single-family house actually rent for today?
questions.why: Two of the eleven paths rank on rent. Right now that ranking rests on the owner's estimate, not on evidence. Get 4 closed comparables plus 2 landlord fee quotes.
questions.where: Broker comp sheet + RentBoard/rent-data cross-check

questions.q: What is the parcel's Tax Rate Area number and the total rate printed on its bill?
questions.why: Santa Clara County publishes 816 TRA rates. The household's own bills imply ~1.33%, which is above the county's city-level summaries, so the difference is either a parcel-specific charge or a data-entry issue. Read it off the bill.
questions.where: Own the tax bill; call Controller-Treasurer Tax Roll Control (408) 808-7979

questions.q: If the heir later wants Property B's rented units for family use or a sale with vacant possession, is an owner-move-in eviction even available on this building?
questions.why: Only one owner-move-in per building is allowed, the unit is then fixed forever as the 'owner's unit', tenants 60+ with 10 years or a catastrophically ill tenant with 5 years cannot be moved, and relocation costs are ~$7,910 per tenant plus $5,280 per protected person. Confirm whether the small-building limits changed after the published page.
questions.where: Rent Ordinance counsel; sf.gov page is the published rule

questions.topic: Leases in place at Property B
questions.q: Copies of both leases, rent roll, security deposits, last rent-increase date and method, and whether the units were ever declared exempt (new construction / substantial rehab).
questions.why: Decides whether rents grow with the market or with the cap, and whether the 60%-of-CPI Rent Board allowance or AB 1482 governs.
questions.where: Property manager file / tenant estoppels

questions.q: Where does the household actually want to live in 2045, and for how many years?
questions.why: Every path in this model is really an occupancy decision wearing a tax costume. If the answer is 'we don't know', the model should be read as a ranking of reversibility, not of return.
questions.where: Household, in writing, before the numbers are argued

questions.q: Does the trust distribute Property A outright, or hold it in a continuing trust? Are there remaindermen, no-contest terms, or a power to appoint?
questions.why: A distribution to the beneficiary is the change in ownership that starts the Prop 19 1-year clock; a continuing trust can delay it and can also forfeit the exclusion.
questions.where: Estate attorney; read the instrument, not the summary

questions.q: What is the gross estate (both properties, cash, retirement, insurance) at date of death, and were there post-1976 taxable gifts?
questions.why: Form 706 is due when the gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts exceeds the basic exclusion - $15,000,000 for a 2026 death. Cash 'considerably' above that threshold is the trigger for real planning, not the houses.
questions.where: CPA with the decedent's Form 709 history

questions.q: Was a portability election made at the first spouse's death (Form 706 Part 6), and is there a DSUE?
questions.why: A DSUE can double the shelter for the surviving spouse. It is only available if a 706 was filed on time (or within the 5-year late relief window for non-filing estates).
questions.where: CPA / prior Form 706

questions.q: Confirm with counsel that California imposes no estate or inheritance tax at the decedent's death in the modelled year.
questions.why: This model assumes 'no CA estate tax'. It is a load-bearing assumption and was NOT confirmed against an official source in this session - it is on the flagged list.
questions.where: CPA; FTB

questions.q: Three written quotes for Property A (owner-occupied) and Property B (3-unit landlord policy), with the dwelling limit, the actual-cash-value vs replacement-cost choice, and the ordinance-or-law upgrade endorsement specified.
questions.why: The household's $1,500/yr guess is used as a placeholder. A $3,000/yr miss is $90,000 over 30 years before inflation, and it lands entirely in the live and rent paths, not the sell path.
questions.where: Independent broker; ask about FAIR Plan as a fallback

questions.q: Sewer scope, roof age, panel/battery status, foundation, permitted status of the third unit at Property B, and a home-inspection-grade capital plan for the next 5 years.
questions.why: The unpermitted-unit question can flip Property B's rental math and its insurability. Capital deferral is the most common way an inherited house loses money.
questions.where: Licensed inspector + SF DBI permit history (public records)

questions.q: Is a like-kind exchange wanted on either sale, and does the heir have investment (not personal) intent for the replacement property?
questions.why: A residence the heir moves into cannot be the replacement property in a 1031 exchange. Deciding this after the sale is decided is usually too late - the identification windows are 45 and 180 days.
questions.where: CPA + qualified intermediary, before listing

questions.q: Sign the criteria page before the projections are circulated: what median-to-median gap, what downside floor, and what reversibility would make each path acceptable?
questions.why: Otherwise the model gets used to justify the answer the household already likes. This is the point of the framework page.
questions.where: Household; see /framework.html

questions.q: What is in the 'considerable amount of money' - cash, taxable brokerage, IRA/401(k), annuity, life insurance - and at what basis?
questions.why: An inherited IRA does not get a step-up and pays ordinary income tax; a brokerage account does get a step-up and can be harvested tax-free. Same dollars, completely different plan.
questions.where: CPA; custodian statements (kept offline)

questions.q: For Property B: does the new Muni parcel tax limit what can be passed to the two sitting tenants, and are those tenancies covered by the Rent Ordinance?
questions.why: The measure text allows a limited pass-through for rent-controlled units. Getting this wrong in either direction changes net operating income and creates Rent Board exposure.
questions.where: Rent counsel; Rent Board petition if needed

questions.q: Is the Property A solar system owned or leased/PPA? What NEM vintage is it on, and what is the true-up treatment of excess credits?
questions.why: A leased or PPA system is a monthly obligation that survives a sale and can block a buyer; an owned system on an older tariff is the reason the electric line is a credit, and that credit does not survive every tariff change.
questions.where: Utility account + contract, kept offline

questions.q: Is Property A split with anyone? If yes: who gets occupancy, who gets rent, how is a buyout priced, and what happens if one owner wants to sell?
questions.why: A partition action, or simply a co-owner who will not sign, is the most common reason an otherwise good plan earns nothing. It also decides whether 'sell in year one' is even available.
questions.where: Household + probate counsel

questions.q: Any federal tax lien, Medi-Cal estate claim, or judgment that would attach before distribution?
questions.why: A Medi-Cal estate claim against the house can consume the equity the whole plan is built on. It must be known before the model, not after.
questions.where: Estate attorney; state recovery unit

suggestions.title: Do not decide 'sell' and 'live' at the same time
suggestions.body: Only 'sell' is irreversible. Live-in for 12-24 months, keep Prop 19 as a live option by occupying and filing for the homeowners' exemption, and decide the sale later with better information. The model prices that option: it is path P-04.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: You pay the reassessment to learn something you could have learned for free.

suggestions.title: Treat the 'rent it' option as a floor, not a plan
suggestions.body: Until four closed leases are on the table, every rent-path number in this workspace is the owner's estimate. Rank the paths again after the comp sheet arrives.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: Path ranking driven by a guess.

suggestions.title: Get the appraisal before the market tells you the price
suggestions.body: A date-of-death appraisal is needed for basis, for the Form 706 (if filed) and for the Prop 19 excess calculation. Same document, three uses, and it is cheapest to obtain once.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: Three different numbers for three different agencies.

suggestions.title: Write the investing policy before the money exists
suggestions.body: Asset allocation, the Treasury parking lane, rebalancing bands, permitted leverage, and the redeployment calendar - agreed and dated now. See /ips.html.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: Proceeds sit in a bank account for a year, or get invested in the month of the funeral.

suggestions.title: Price occupancy explicitly with imputed rent
suggestions.body: Living in Property A is not free and renting it is not pure profit. The imputed-rent line puts the same dollar on both sides so the paths are compared like-for-like.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: The live path looks 40% better than it is.

suggestions.title: Recheck the law once a year, on a fixed date
suggestions.body: Prop 19's indexed amount re-publishes every other February 16; SF's tax rate is adopted each summer; parcel taxes change with ballots; the federal exclusion indexes annually. See /recheck.html and /watch.html.

suggestions.title: Distinguish 'enacted' from 'proposed' in every table
suggestions.body: Each rule row carries a status: enacted (with effective date) or proposed (with sponsor and stage). The Prop H row is the live example: approved by voters on 2026-11-03 but not certified until 2026-12-03 and not billed until FY 2027-28.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: Modelling a bill as if it were law.

suggestions.title: Keep the private numbers out of this repository
suggestions.body: This site publishes rounded, anonymised figures only. Statements, appraisals, leases, accounts and the APN belong in the offline folder, not in git history - history is forever and search indexes it.

suggestions.title: Run the tax sale in the same year as the death
suggestions.body: A sale in the year of death uses the stepped-up basis immediately: little or no gain. This is modelled as P-06 and it is the cheapest tax outcome in the whole set - which is exactly why the non-tax reasons have to be argued explicitly rather than assumed away.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: Holding for 20 years converts a tax-free gain into a taxable one.

suggestions.title: Add a liquidity floor before any illiquid choice
suggestions.body: Two houses plus a fixed income is a fragile balance sheet. Set the floor (24 months of all carrying costs plus a capital-events reserve) in the IPS and make the paths satisfy it before comparing returns.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: A forced sale in a bad year.

suggestions.title: Do not let one projection set the answer
suggestions.body: Compare all paths on ranges, all on the same transfer date and the same horizons, and re-run annually. If the recommendation flips when a range moves, the honest conclusion is 'not sensitive enough to decide yet', and the open-questions page says so.

suggestions.title: Separate the three tax systems in the write-up
suggestions.body: Estate tax (transfer at death), income tax (basis and gain), and property tax (assessment) have different rules, different deadlines and different authorities. Every table on this site labels which of the three it is talking about.
suggestions.risk_if_skipped: The classic error: assuming a step-up lowers the property tax bill, or that Prop 19 lowers income tax.

flags.item: Property B: tax-to-assessment ratio does not reconcile
flags.detail: The household's own 2025 figures for Property B (tax $2,440 on assessed value $114,250) imply a 2.14% rate. San Francisco's published FY 2026-27 secured rate is 1.18162182%. A ~2x gap means either (a) the 'tax' line includes non-ad-valorem special assessments or supplemental/escape amounts, or (b) the assessed value quoted is net of an exemption while the tax is computed on a different base. Nothing in this model depends on the answer, but the Property B carrying-cost line does.
flags.action: Pull three years of SF bills and the parcel record (Treasurer portal, offline); reconcile line by line.

flags.item: Property A: implied rate above the city summaries
flags.detail: The household's bills imply 1.30%-1.35% of assessed value for 2014-2025, while the county's FY 2025-26 compilation shows a 1.00000% maximum levy plus bond lines that sum to roughly 1.04%-1.06% before school-district bonds. The parcel's own tax rate area total was not read from the rate book in this pass (Section III covers 816 TRAs).
flags.action: Read the TRA number off the bill and look it up in the county Tax Rate Book, Section III. Model uses 1.334% until then.

flags.item: Homeowners and landlord insurance premium is an owner guess
flags.detail: The $1,500/yr figure supplied for both properties was not confirmable from an official source. Published state-level averages for the 2025 experience year (California Department of Insurance data call, as reported by secondary sources) are materially higher for the homeowners market and higher again for FAIR Plan dwelling fire.
flags.action: Three written quotes per property; replace the placeholder and re-run. Flagged, not filled in.

flags.item: Market rent for Property A is unverified
flags.detail: No comparable lease evidence exists yet. The rent paths are therefore reported as a floor, not a forecast.
flags.action: Broker comp sheet for the ZIP, 4 closed leases, 2025-26 rent board/ab1482 status check.

flags.item: the city's utility rates not read from an official rate sheet
flags.detail: Water $100-$150/month and the solar electricity credit are household-supplied. The City of The city's current rate resolution was not located and read in this session.
flags.action: The city's utility rate sheet; PG&E bill for 12 months of true-up history.

flags.item: 'California has no estate tax' was not verified this session
flags.detail: The model assumes no California estate or inheritance tax at death. This is a load-bearing assumption and is stated as unverified rather than asserted as fact.
flags.action: CPA confirmation with citation; update row 4 of /tax-rules.html and re-run.

flags.detail: Voter-approved 2026-11-03 per preliminary counts (74.4% yes as reported); county certification due 2026-12-03; first bills FY 2027-28. Treated as 'approved, pending certification' throughout.
flags.action: Confirm certification on 2026-12-04 and replace the flag with the ordinance number.

flags.item: Inflation baseline is an assumption, not a source
flags.detail: Long-run inflation (1.5%/2.5%/3.8%) drives every nominal series on this site. No official CPI series was read in this session (FRED CSV endpoints were not reachable from the build environment).
flags.action: Replace with a BLS CPI-U annual-average table read directly, then re-run the sensitivity grid.

flags.item: Equity and bill-return history is academic, not governmental
flags.detail: 1928-2025 S&P 500 total returns and 3-month bill returns come from the NYU Stern table. It is a standard, citable academic source but it is not an official statistic, and the Black-Swan section depends on it.
flags.action: Spot-check 1929-1932 and 2007-2009 against a Federal Reserve or BLS publication before the IPS is signed.

flags.item: Documentary transfer tax exemption list for the trust distribution
flags.detail: Rev. & Tax. Code 11911 sets the rate; the death/gift non-application is cited by county recorders to Rev. & Tax. Code 11930. The Santa Clara County ordinance text itself was not read in this session.
flags.action: Escrow/title company to confirm in writing before the deed is recorded.

flags.item: Repo history contained no pre-rounding data
flags.detail: At session start this branch held exactly one commit (a 5,900-byte README and one 11-byte file). There is no earlier public-data exposure inside this repository to scrub, and no un-rounded figures were ever committed here.
flags.action: None possible in-repo. The exposure risk lives in the *other* repository found during research (see handoff notes) - if that repo is ours, its history must be rebuilt or the repo deleted; deleting a branch does not delete the objects.

flags.item: Non-ad-valorem charges on Property A modelled as zero
flags.detail: The Santa Clara Valley Water District parcel charge and any other direct assessments are billed on the tax bill but are not value-based, so they are not in the 1% levy or in the rate book's ad valorem columns. The engine carries $0 for them, which understates A's carrying cost by roughly the amount the county's own summary and the household's bill disagree by (see F-2).
flags.action: Read the parcel charge schedule at scvwd.gov and the 'Special Assessments' lines on the actual bill; enter the flat amount in inputs.py as a separate line, not inside the rate.

flags.detail: Rental losses are modelled as suspended (not deductible against salary) and the real estate professional exception as unavailable. Both are likely at this income level, but the phase-out runs from $100,000 to $150,000 of modified AGI and the household's actual position is unknown. If losses were deductible, the rent paths improve materially.
flags.action: CPA to confirm in writing; then re-run with the toggle on the what-if page.

laws.rule: Unified estate/gift tax; basic exclusion amount
laws.detail: Filing threshold by year of death, as published: 2024 $13,610,000; 2025 $13,990,000; 2026 $15,000,000. Top rate 40% above the threshold. Portability of the unused exclusion (DSUE) requires a timely Form 706.
laws.watch: Any bill changing the exclusion or the 40% rate. No pending measure was verified in this session - do not model one.

laws.rule: California estate tax / inheritance tax
laws.detail: This model assumes California imposes NO estate or inheritance tax. That is the conventional position and it matches the FTB materials reviewed, but no official source was read that states it in terms. Flagged (F-6) because it is load-bearing for the 'considerable cash' side of the plan.
laws.watch: Ask the CPA to put the 'no CA estate tax' conclusion in writing with a citation.

laws.rule: Basis step-up at death (IRC 1014)
laws.detail: Basis becomes fair market value at the date of death (or the alternate valuation date if elected and it lowers the estate tax). This is why a sale in the year of death usually produces little or no gain - and it has NOTHING to do with the property tax bill.
laws.watch: Repeal or limitation of the step-up has been proposed in past Congresses and never enacted; nothing verified as pending now.

laws.rule: Long-term capital gains rates + net investment income tax
laws.detail: 2025/2026 published bands 0% / 15% / 20%; the 20% band begins above $533,400 (single) / $600,050 (married filing jointly). Unrecaptured section 1250 gain on depreciation is capped at 25%. NIIT of 3.8% applies above modified AGI thresholds.
laws.watch: Watch the NIIT thresholds and any surtax proposal; the model adds 3.8% to gains.

laws.rule: No preferential rate for capital gains
laws.detail: FTB, verbatim position: 'California does not have a lower rate for capital gains. All capital gains are taxed as ordinary income.' This is why a $2.5M gain costs far more here than the federal tables suggest.
laws.watch: No change verified.

laws.rule: Mental/Behavioral Health Services Tax: 1% on taxable income over $1,000,000
laws.detail: Read as line 62 of the 2024 Form 540 booklet: 1% of the amount by which CA taxable income exceeds $1,000,000 reduced by certain credits. The threshold is NOT indexed. Applied in the model on top of the 12.3% top rate for every sale year in which a large gain is recognised.
laws.watch: Recheck with the 2026 booklet when posted; confirm whether the threshold indexes.

laws.rule: Section 121 principal-residence exclusion
laws.detail: $250,000 single / $500,000 married filing jointly of gain, requiring ownership AND use as principal residence for 2 of the last 5 years. Inherited property usually qualifies only if the heir moves in - which is why 'live first, sell later' is a separate path (P-04, P-09, P-11).
laws.watch: No change verified.

laws.rule: Depreciation of residential rental property: 27.5 years straight line, mid-month
laws.detail: Only the building (land excluded) is depreciable, and only while held for rent. Every dollar claimed reduces the gain on sale - the deferral is real, the bill is too. Modelled with a 75% building allocation, which is an assumption (F-7).
laws.watch: No change verified.

laws.rule: Proposition 13: acquisition base year, factored at CPI or 2%, whichever is lower
laws.detail: Reaffirmed in the county's FY 2025-26 rate book. The 2% cap is what the model uses for every future year, including high-inflation years - that is the conservative (low tax) side of the assumption for the 'keep' paths.
laws.watch: No change verified.

laws.rule: Proposition 19 parent-child exclusion, R&TC 63.2
laws.detail: New taxable value = prior factored base year value + any market value above (prior FBYV + indexed allowance). Published allowance: $1,000,000 -> $1,022,600 -> $1,044,590 for transfers 2025-02-16 to 2027-02-15, indexed biennially by the California FHFA house-price index. Conditions: prior principal residence, heir's principal residence, homeowners'-exemption claim within 1 year, BOE-19-P within 3 years. Income use (rental) voids it entirely.
laws.watch: Next allowance publication expected 2027-02-16; a restoration of the full exclusion for all property types has been proposed in the Legislature (Prop 15 lineage) and has not passed - do not model it.

laws.rule: County documentary transfer tax, R&TC 11911
laws.detail: $0.55 per $500 of consideration (0.11%), measured on the price EXCLUSIVE of debt that stays with the property. A city may add one-half of the county amount and the county credits it. No municipal add-on was identified in the FY 2025-26 compilation (F-11: confirm with escrow).
laws.watch: A gift or transfer at death is not a sale; counties rely on R&TC 11930 to exempt it. 11930's text was not read this session (F-10) - get escrow's written confirmation.

laws.rule: San Francisco real property transfer tax (cliff tiers per $500)
laws.detail: $2.50 up to $250k; $3.40 to $1M; $3.75 to $5M; $11.25 to $10M; $27.50 to $25M; $30.00 above. The tier applies to the ENTIRE consideration, so it is a cliff, not a marginal schedule - a 1% price move can cost thousands. Exemptions include transfer to spouse/domestic partner, gift, transfer at death, and reconveyance to a trust the grantor owns. Owner-occupied realty for a resident is capped at 3.75 (Admin Code 1108.6).
laws.watch: Proposition I (2026) would have redirected half of this tax to affordable housing; it FAILED, so the tier table stands.

laws.rule: Proposition H Muni parcel tax (multifamily)
laws.detail: Approved 2026-11-03 with 74.4% (245,712 yes / 84,456 no). Multifamily: $250 base for the first 5,000 sq ft plus $0.195 per additional sq ft, capped at $50,000; 15 years starting July 2027; results certified by 2026-12-03; first bills FY 2027-28. Landlords may pass through no more than 50%, capped at $65 per unit, only where the rent was set before 2027-06-01.
laws.watch: Certification is the only remaining step; after that it is a cost in every Property B path and must be re-read when the first bills issue.

laws.rule: Proposition RTM regional transit assessment (1 cent SF / half cent SCC)
laws.detail: Approved 2026-11-03; collection begins April 2027. It is a sales/use tax surcharge, so it raises the cost of every appliance, roof and repair in the capital plan rather than the property tax.
laws.watch: Confirm the start month before pricing the 5-year capital plan.

laws.rule: Measure S parcel fee (Safe, Clean Water and Flood Protection)
laws.detail: Approved November 2020, no expiry date, adjusts up to 2% a year, billed as a line on the property tax bill. This is the most likely reason the household's bills imply a rate above the county's 1% levy (F-2). Modelled as a separate $0 for now and flagged, because the per-parcel charge for this parcel was not read.
laws.watch: Read the district's current parcel-charge schedule and put the actual number here.

laws.rule: AB 1482 rent cap: 5% + CPI, maximum 10%; just-cause eviction
laws.detail: Used in the model only as an UPPER BOUND on assumed rent growth for covered units, and to justify a 5% vacancy/turn allowance. The statute text (Civ. Code 1947.12) was not read this session, and the local CPI ordinance for Santa Clara County was not obtained (F-3).
laws.expires: 2030-01-01 (an expiry is stated in the summaries; not verified)
laws.watch: The 2030 expiry is the single most consequential tenant-law date for the rent paths.

laws.rule: Owner move-in eviction, Rent Ordinance 37.9(a)(11) and 37.9C relocation
laws.detail: One owner-move-in per building; the heir must move in within 3 months and live there 36 continuous months; 25% ownership minimum; tenants aged 60+ with 10 years' tenancy (or catastrophically ill with 5) cannot be moved out of a 2+ unit building. Relocation per the latest table read: $7,910 per tenant, $23,730 per unit maximum, plus $5,280 for each elderly/disabled/minor household member with NO cap on the extras (notices served 2024-03-01 to 2025-02-28).
laws.watch: The 2025-03-01 onward schedule was not located - do not rely on the dollar amounts without re-reading the current Form 579 (F-4).

laws.rule: Change in ownership on sale of a leased property, R&TC 61
laws.detail: A transfer of the lessor's interest in a lease with a remaining term UNDER 35 years IS a change in ownership: selling Property B with tenants in place reassesses it in full. That is a property-tax consequence of the 'sell B' paths that most analyses miss.
laws.watch: No change verified.

laws.rule: Passive activity losses and the $25,000 allowance phase-out
laws.detail: The model treats rental losses as SUSPENDED rather than deductible against salary, and treats the real estate professional exception as unavailable. That is conservative for the rent paths. Phase-out runs from $100,000 to $150,000 modified AGI.
laws.watch: Have the CPA confirm the household's actual position; it changes the rent paths materially (F-13).

laws.rule: Like-kind exchange (IRC 1031) for rental property
laws.detail: Available only for property held for investment or business use - never for the principal residence, and never for Property A if the heir lives in it. Defers gain and carries the low basis forward; combined with a fresh Prop 13 base at the replacement property it can be the cheapest option, but it locks in illiquidity. Decision and written advice must be obtained BEFORE a sale (see Q-14).
laws.watch: Recurring proposals to limit or repeal 1031.

criteria.purpose: Fix the thresholds that make each choice correct, in writing, before arguing about any projection. If a projection moves and the thresholds still hold, the answer has not changed.
live: The household intends Property A to be their principal residence for at least 5 years (that is what makes Prop 19 and later section 121 real, and what justifies the reassessment).
Gross rental yield on A is BELOW the after-tax yield available on Treasury bills - i.e. the rental market is not paying them enough to give up the liquidity.
Written insurance quotes for the owner-occupied house are below the modelled figure, and the 5-year capital plan needs under $150,000.
No co-beneficiary needs cash, and no creditor or Medi-Cal claim can attach to the house.
They can fund the annual shortfall between A's carrying cost and Property B's net operating income without borrowing.
rent: Four closed leases for comparable Santa Clara County single-family houses show net yield (after tax, insurance, upkeep, vacancy and management) above the after-tax yield on Treasuries by at least 0.5 percentage points.
The household accepts that a non-owner-occupied inherited house gets NO Prop 19 exclusion: the model's rent paths therefore carry a fully reassessed tax bill from year one.
Depreciation is wanted, and the household has read the recapture line in this workspace and accepts the deferred-tax trade.
The rental losses will be suspended under the passive rules - i.e. there is no salary offset.
sell: Net after-tax proceeds would produce more income in a diversified portfolio than the house produces net, at the household's own risk tolerance, for the whole planning horizon.
The household needs liquidity, wants to consolidate debt, or a co-owner requires cash.
Expected carrying costs plus the reassessment penalty exceed the rent they can actually prove.
They will not live in it - in which case Prop 19 is unavailable and the tax argument for holding collapses.
mixed: Occupancy is uncertain, or the housing/rent evidence is still thin: live in A, claim the exemption and the exclusion, and defer the sale decision by 24-36 months. This keeps every door open, costs only the option's own carrying cost, and it is the only path that preserves both Prop 19 and section 121.
hard_stops: Any Medi-Cal estate claim, tax lien or judgment against the property.
An unpermitted unit at Property B that the insurer or a buyer will not accept.
A co-owner who will not sign (partition risk).
A liquidity shortfall that forces a sale in whatever year it happens.
criteria.tie_break: If two paths are within 10% of each other on real terminal wealth, choose the more reversible one. Reversibility is worth more than a modelling margin.

decisions.decision: Publish only rounded figures; keep the raw numbers offline
decisions.rationale: The household's exact tax bills and rent roll are traceable through public records. Every dollar figure in this repository passes through a $10 rounding step, and no address, APN or account number is stored here.

decisions.decision: Rank paths on real terminal wealth, with use value shown separately
decisions.rationale: Wealth and utility are different things. Folding imputed rent into the objective function would let a lifestyle preference drive a financial recommendation. It is now a reported column and an explicit toggle, never silent.

decisions.decision: Treat path cash flow at the risk-free opportunity cost, not at a borrowing rate
decisions.rationale: Every path is funded the same way, so the comparison is clean. Charging the live-in paths a consumer-loan spread for a shortfall they would actually fund from savings or salary would have biased the answer toward selling. Stated as a convention.

decisions.decision: Treat rental losses as suspended (no salary offset)
decisions.rationale: Conservative for the rent paths, and the likely legal outcome at this income level. Marked for CPA confirmation as L-19 / F-13.

decisions.decision: Do not model any un-enacted legislation
decisions.rationale: Proposed bills appear on /watch.html with their status and nothing else. A plan built on a bill that has not passed is a wager, not a plan.

decisions.decision: Leave unconfirmable figures blank rather than estimating them
decisions.rationale: municipal utility rates, the CPI series, the 2025-26 Form 579 amounts and the parcel's tax rate area could not be read from an official source in this session. They are blank + flagged, and the affected rows say so.

decisions.decision: Keep the 2045 transfer year as the shared comparison date
decisions.rationale: The trust transfer window is 2040-2050. A single mid-point date is used so all twelve paths are compared like-for-like; the what-if page lets the date move, and the sensitivity to it is published.

glossary.defn: What you 'paid' for tax purposes: stepped-up value at death, plus capital improvements, minus depreciation claimed. Gain = net sale price - adjusted basis.
'According to value' - a tax computed as a percentage of assessed value, as opposed to a flat parcel charge.
An estate-tax election to value assets 6 months after death instead of at death. It lowers the estate tax only if values fell - and it lowers the heir's basis by the same amount.
The federal estate/gift threshold above which the 40% estate tax applies ($15,000,000 for a 2026 death).
Resampling in fixed-length contiguous blocks instead of single years, so a simulated path keeps real sequences of bad years together. Used here with 3-year blocks.
The claim form that actually starts the Proposition 19 parent-child exclusion. Filing the homeowners' exemption is NOT the same filing.
The property-tax event that resets a base year value. A distribution under a trust can be one; whether it is depends on who holds what before and after.
A deceased spouse's unused estate-tax exclusion, transferable to the surviving spouse - but only if a Form 706 was filed to elect it.
Seller-paid credits at closing. Modelled as a percentage of price so the number survives re-pricing.
A parcel's Prop 13 base, grown each year by CPI or 2%, whichever is lower. This - not market value - drives the bill on an unchanged property.
The market rent an owner-occupier avoids by living in their own house. It is the price of occupying the asset, so a 'live there' path is not free.
Residential depreciation starts (and stops) as if in the middle of the month, so a December purchase gets half a month of it.
Net investment income tax - 3.8% on investment income including capital gains above modified AGI thresholds. It stacks on top of the 20% rate, not instead of it.
A flat parcel charge (water district, flood control, some bonds) billed on the tax bill regardless of value. The likeliest explanation of both properties' odd implied rates.
A San Francisco no-fault eviction allowing an owner with 25%+ ownership to take one unit for their own use, subject to a 36-month occupancy promise and relocation payments.
What a future dollar is worth today at a chosen discount rate. Used here to make 30-year streams comparable; the discount rate itself is an assumption on the what-if page.
Nominal is dollars; real is dollars divided by prices. Two properties and a stock portfolio are only comparable in real terms.
Depreciation you took is taxed again on sale at up to 25% - a rate that exists specifically because the underlying gain would otherwise be taxed at 20%.
San Francisco's real property transfer tax, payable at recording, with tiered cliff rates.
$250,000 (single) of gain on a principal residence, needing 2 of the last 5 years of both ownership and use. Inherited houses usually fail the 'use' test until someone moves in.
The same average return producing very different outcomes depending on the ORDER of the years. It is the whole reason a sale at 2045 might be staged.
A passive rental loss the tax law will not let you deduct now; it waits, unused, until there is passive income or a sale.
A catch-up bill issued after a reassessment, for the part-year already billed at the old value. Two of them typically follow a change in ownership.
The parcel-level map code that determines which voter-approved bonds add on top of the 1% levy. Santa Clara County has 816 of them.
Holding sale proceeds in 3-month to 2-year Treasuries for a fixed period before buying risk assets, so a crash just after the sale cannot hit the whole stake at once.
The benefit of consuming the housing yourself, as opposed to the money it could earn. Reported separately here, and never used silently.
A haircut on gross rent for empty periods and re-letting costs; 5% is used in this model as an assumption, not a measurement.

process.title: Before the death - the trust route
process.body: Nothing in this list requires probate if the house is titled in the trust. Confirm with the estate attorney that Property A is in the trust NOW, that the trust is revocable and the settlor is the occupant, and who the successor trustees are. If the house is not in the trust, the timeline below is optimistic by 12-18 months.

process.title: At the death - documents to obtain
process.body: Certified death certificates (several), the trust instrument and any amendments, the trailer/assignment of personal property, the property's most recent tax bill and assessment record, the mortgage statement (if any), the insurance policy, and the utility accounts. Everything else follows from these.

process.title: Valuation - the single most load-bearing document
process.body: Commission a written, dated appraisal of Property A at the date of death (and of the contents if material). It sets income-tax basis, the Form 706 number if one is filed, and the Prop 19 excess calculation. Get it from a licensed appraiser, not an estate agent's market analysis, and keep the unrounded copy offline.

process.title: Estate tax decision
process.body: Add the gross estate plus post-1976 taxable gifts. If it exceeds the threshold for the year of death ($15,000,000 for 2026), Form 706 is due nine months after death, on extension via Form 4768. Even when no tax is due, file 706 if portability of a prior spouse's unused exclusion is wanted.

process.title: Distribution and the change in ownership
process.body: The trustee's distribution to the beneficiary is the property-tax event. File the change in ownership statement (BOE-502-D) within 150 days. Expect supplemental bills afterwards - they are for the part-year, not a mistake.

process.title: Property tax: two claims, two deadlines
process.body: If the heir will live there: (a) file for the homeowners' exemption within ONE year, and (b) file the BOE-19-P parent-child claim within THREE years (or before any transfer to a third party). Miss (a) and (b) is void. If the heir will rent it, do not file them - the exclusion is unavailable and the value reassesses in full.

process.title: Insurance and utilities from the date of distribution
process.body: Notify the insurer (vacancy changes the policy), re-title the utility accounts, and if the solar system is leased/PPA find out whether the contract is assignable before listing.

process.title: Choose a path against the written criteria
process.body: Not against the projection. The criteria on /framework.html were agreed before the numbers; score each path against them, then look at the money. Record the choice and the date in the decision log.

process.title: If selling: price, then stage, then invest per the IPS
process.body: Decide the 1031 question in writing BEFORE listing. Then follow the investment policy - the Treasury parking lane and the phase-in calendar - which was agreed while there was nothing to argue about.

process.title: After: re-run once a year
process.body: /recheck.html and /watch.html. The transfer may be 15+ years away; the rules in this workspace will not all still be true in 2045, and some will have changed by 2028.
